Careful. I'm past the stage of politely declining things, %1$s.
Then I'll ask, which is more than I've managed with anyone else.
Thank you. Everyone says it; you're one of the few who paused first.
So am I, on the good days, and I've decided to count those double.
That's kind. I'll take kind — I've had a great deal of advice instead.
I intend to.
Finally, somebody sensible.
It is. Off you go, %1$s.
Frightened and pleased at the same hour, which nobody warns you about.
Well enough. Better than my mother had it, and she never let me forget hers.
Some mornings I can't lace my own boots. The rest of it I'd not trade.
No, and I'm told that's usual. It hasn't stopped me lying awake about it.
Ready as a house half-built. It'll have to finish itself around us.
I was ready in spring. Now I'm just impatient, which I'm told is the next stage.
Sleep, and nobody's yet worked out how to carry that up the lane.
Wool, if you're offering. Everything I've knitted so far has been the wrong size.
Someone to take the heavy end of things without making a speech about it.
Tired in a way I don't mind, which is new. Ask me again at the end of the week.
Large, mostly. And hungry at hours that don't have names yet.
Two of us in here, %1$s, and only one of us sleeps. I'll let you guess which.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.fine.admi: That's the useful kind of promise. Thank you.
Around. Aye. That'll do more than advice would.
Good. I'll hold you to being nearby, %1$s.
Since about the spring, if I'm honest. It crept.
Long enough that 'fine' stopped being a lie and started being a habit.
Longer than I'd care to say stood up, %1$s.
Thank you. That's the right amount of fuss.
So I've found. Don't. But don't forget, either.
...Nobody asks it like that. Give me a day and I'll have an answer.
Nothing dramatic. Somebody asking twice, mostly. You've done that.
Company, and not being handled. You've managed both, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.fine.blun: ...No. I'm not. Nobody's ever just said it, so I've been getting away with 'fine' for weeks.
That's very direct. ...And correct, %1$s, which is the annoying part.
Hm. Well. You've saved us both about four more rounds of me saying 'fine', I suppose.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.fine.clos: It wasn't a bad question. It just had one answer.
Ha. Now we're both being reasonable and it's very unsettling.
...Aye, well. Ask me a better one and I'll do better, %1$s.
Then I've been short with you for no reason. It happens.
Listening's not nothing. I'll bear it in mind, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.fine.dig/: ...Mostly. There's a thing, but it's small and it'll keep.
You're not letting that pass, are you. ...No. Not entirely.
Really. Ask me again in a week and I might have a longer answer.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.fine.dism: ...You asked how I was. That's how I am.
Not everything needs to be a story, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.fine.foll: Bread on time and nobody dying. That's the whole recipe.
Routine, mostly. Say it out loud and it sounds grim, but it isn't.
Small things done properly, %1$s. Nothing you'd write down.
So it is. Off you go.
You look like it, if you don't mind me saying.
Then stand here a while. It's catching, apparently.
Ha. You've had the interesting kind, have you, %1$s?
From your mouth to the weather's ear.
It won't. But it's good of you to say.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.fine.glad: It isn't, is it. Steady's the best most weeks manage.
Quite. I'll take steady over interesting.
Kind of you to count it as something.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.fine.open: ...It's my brother. That's all you're getting today.
Nothing I can put in a sentence yet, %1$s. That's why it keeps.
You'll hear it eventually. Not stood up, though.
So I've found. Thank you for that.
...That's the right way round. Nearly everyone wants it now.
I might. That's more than I'd have said last month.
Just so. And I'll remember you offered, %1$s.
...No. It isn't. Thank you for not making me argue that.
Everyone keeps calling it small. Including me. It helps to hear otherwise.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.fine/1: Same as ever, thanks for asking. Ups and downs, mostly evens. That's village life.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.fine/2: Steady enough. No news worth the word, which is its own kind of good, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.fine/3: Oh, plodding along. The bell rings, the bread bakes, I complain, I sleep. Comforting, really.
...Get away from me, %1$s.
That's life. Aye. Say that to the family.
I know people die. I knew this one.
Thank you. Everyone wants the story. You didn't ask for it.
That's a kindness. I'll come find you when I can say it.
Good. Sitting here quietly is the most anyone's helped this week.
...It was. Go on, then. I'll not hold it forever.
True enough, it was. Say nothing else and we'll call it managed.
...Thank you. Now leave it, %1$s.
Comfort. Is that what that was.
Then say the comfort next time and leave the philosophy at home.
...I'll take that it wasn't meant to land like it did, %1$s.
Do.
True enough.
Good.
Quite. Thank you for stopping at all.
Go on. It's not a day for company.
Mind how you go.
I will. Don't come looking first.
It is. It might be a while, %1$s.
...I'll try. That's the honest version.
So I've found. Thank you.
Mind how you go.
We'll speak again, %1$s.
The animals, then. And don't tell me you've done it.
If you must do something, do that. It helps me not to be asked.
Just so. Quietly, mind.
...Good.
Thank you. Stand where I can see you and don't talk.
That's the most useful thing anyone's offered this week, %1$s.
...They were loud. Nobody says that at a funeral, but they were, and I miss it.
They'd have hated the fuss. That's the bit that keeps getting me, %1$s.
Give me a moment. ...No. Not today. But ask me again.
So it is. Thank you for asking at all.
Leave it there, %1$s.
Away you go.
The animals. Nobody thinks of the animals. If you would.
There's a fence I've not touched in a week. It'd be a mercy, honestly.
...Aye. There is. I'll show you tomorrow, %1$s.
...Aye. Do that.
You don't have to say anything. That's the whole of what I want.
Sit, then. It's better than the house, %1$s.
...Don't. If you're kind about it now I'll not get through the rest of the day. ...But aye. Thank you. Say nothing else.
I'm allowed. I know I'm allowed. Knowing and feeling are two different counties, %1$s.
Right. Yes. Fine. ...You're the first who didn't tell me it gets easier, so — thank you for that.
...Aye. I am allowed, aren't I. Nobody's said that.
Everyone's telling me to be strong. You didn't. Thank you.
Allowed. That's the whole of what I needed to hear, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.grieving/: Ah. You heard, then. We lost one of our own. The whole village feels the gap. ...Thank you for asking, %1$s.
It's been a mournful few days here. Someone's chair sits empty. I keep expecting them round the corner.
There's grief in the streets just now. We hold each other up when it comes. Kind of you to notice, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.guarded.f: Another day. You'd be surprised how many people don't leave that door open.
True enough. Ask me in a month and you may get a longer answer than this one.
That suits me. I warm slowly and I've never apologised for it.
Then we understand each other, which is a fair start on its own.
Good. The ones who take offence at it are the ones I was right about.
That's the first sensible thing anyone has said to me about it, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.guarded.l: Right. Has the rain reached your side of the village yet?
Very well. What's your opinion of the new gate? Everyone else has one.
Easier. Where were you before here? That's a question I can hear the answer to.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.guarded.p: Nothing that's yours yet. Ask again in a year and you may have earned it.
That's the second time today. I'll give the same answer and enjoy it less.
No. I gave you the polite version and you've spent it.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.guarded.r: ...Thank you. People generally push, and then wonder why I stay short with them.
That's noted, and it counts for more than the answer you were after.
Then I'll tell you this much: it's been a long month and it isn't over.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.guarded.t: ...That's an unfair tactic and it's working. Go on, then.
I've not been offered that before. Alright — a sentence each, and no more.
It helps. I'll match whatever you give me and not a word past it.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.guarded/1: Well enough, thank you. And yourself?
dialogue.conversations.noticed.guarded/2: Fine. It's not a question I'd usually answer at length.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.guarded/3: Same as ever. That's most of what I give out to people I've not known long.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.hurt.dism: Then you've a poor eye for scratches. Good day to you.
It's my scratch, and I'll decide how much of one it is.
Right. I'll remember that the next time you want telling how you are.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.hurt.foll: Then I'll still be here, and I'll be less pleasant about it. Come anyway.
You'd best, because I'll not send for anyone myself. I never do.
That's the useful sort of kindness. Everyone offers sympathy; nobody comes back.
...Go on, then. Don't talk at me and we'll get along fine.
You don't have to. But sit, and I'll stop pretending to be busy.
That's the first offer today that didn't come with advice attached.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.hurt.rest: The work doesn't rest, so neither do I. That's how it's always gone here.
You're right and I'll ignore you, which is what I do with everyone who's right.
Say that to whoever's expecting me at the gate and I'll go and lie down gladly.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.hurt.tend: I've bound it myself, badly, and I'll not hear a word about that.
The cleric looked at it and made a face. That's all the treatment I've had.
Not yet. Everyone here is busy and I'm bad at asking, which is a poor pairing.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.hurt.what: Something came out of the dark faster than I did. That's the whole story.
My own fault. I went where I'd been told not to go and the telling was right.
A fall, and a stupid one. I'd rather it had been something with a story in it.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.hurt/1: Been better. I took a bad one two nights back and it hasn't finished with me yet.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.hurt/2: Sore, if you want the truth of it. I'm walking it off and it isn't working.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.hurt/3: In myself? In myself I'm fine. It's the rest of me that's the problem, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.proud.dis: It wasn't nothing to me. But I'll forget it if you'd rather.
Then I'll keep the next one in my head where it can't be waved off.
Fine. That's twice today somebody has told me my own feelings were wrong.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.proud.emb: Nothing. That's the trick of it — you're allowed to just hear it.
Neither did I, so I said it badly. It still counts.
Stand there a moment and let it be true. That's all that's wanted, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.proud.fol: Then I've said it too rarely, and I'll do something about that.
Good. I nearly kept it to myself, the way I keep most things.
It cost me nothing and it seems to have been worth a great deal. I'll remember that.
I held a lantern and complained. Let's not rewrite it into a partnership.
That's generous and about a third true, which is the good kind of generous.
Take the credit, %1$s. It's not so heavy that you need help carrying it.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.proud.wha: You finished the thing you said you'd finish. You'd be amazed how rare that is.
You did it without being asked twice, and without telling everyone afterwards.
You took a problem off me that I'd stopped believing anyone would take.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.proud.who: Anyone who slowed down near me. Two of them twice, I think.
The baker, at length, and she'd not asked. She knows now.
Enough people that you'll be greeted oddly for a week. You've earned it.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.proud/1: Better than I've been in a while, and you're a good part of the reason, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.proud/2: Pleased. Quietly, and about something you did, which I'd rather say now than never.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.proud/3: Good. I've been telling people about that thing you finished, and I've not been brief.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.resume.ho: Stiff in the morning and forgotten by noon. That's the shape of getting better.
The same, which after three weeks means worse. I've an appointment with the cleric.
Better than it looks. It looks appalling, so that's a low bar to clear.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.resume.il: Then say a day and keep to it. A regular thing is only regular if it has a name.
Careful — I'll come to depend on it, and depending on people is a habit I lost.
That's more than the cleric offered, and the cleric is paid for it.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.resume.le: Do. I'll say if it changes, and I'll say plainly.
Right. It's mine to carry and it's lighter for having been said out loud.
Then it's mine again. That's how it should be, and thank you for the loan.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.resume.so: Then come now and we'll say no more about it. That's the whole of the apology I want.
People don't say that. They explain instead, and the explaining is what stings.
Accepted, and I mean it. I've done the same to somebody and never gone back.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.resume.th: You asked. People who ask get told; it isn't more complicated than that.
It costs me nothing and it seems to be worth something. I'll go on doing it.
That's the second time you've thanked me for a thing I'd have done anyway.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.resume/1: You came back. I'd bet against it, quietly, and I'm glad to have lost.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.resume/2: You said you'd look in. You didn't, and I'd rather say so than pretend I didn't notice.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.resume/3: It's mending. Slowly, and mending, and you're the only one who's asked twice.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.worn.back: So it is. Thank you for asking at all.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.worn.dism: I have been getting on with it. That's the entire problem.
Right. That's why I said fine to the last four people who asked.
Then I'll go and be tired somewhere you're not.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.worn.foll: A whole day. I'd not know what to do with one, but I'll find out.
You mean that, don't you. Nobody's offered and I'd stopped expecting it.
Then I'll take it, and I'll not spend it usefully, and that's the point.
True enough. Thank you for asking.
I've been carrying it on my own so long I'd forgotten there was another way.
...Right. I'll try to remember you said that on the next bad morning.
That's the sentence I needed and couldn't have asked anyone for. Thank you.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.worn.how_: Since the spring, and I only noticed it in the autumn. That's how it goes.
Long enough that I've stopped calling it a bad patch and started calling it me.
I couldn't tell you. There wasn't a day it started; it just kept not stopping.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.worn.no_f: ...No. But everyone wants one, and I've been inventing them to be polite.
That's the first time this month somebody hasn't tried to solve me.
Then I'll stop hunting for one. It's tiring work on top of tired.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.worn.take: The evening rounds, if you're serious. That's the hour that finishes me.
Nothing you could lift. It's not the weight, it's that there's no end to it.
The asking helps more than the taking would, which I didn't expect to say.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.worn/1: Tired. Not the kind that sleep fixes, before you offer.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.worn/2: Worn through, if I'm honest. Nothing's wrong. I'm just at the end of myself.
dialogue.conversations.noticed.worn/3: I've been better, %1$s, and I couldn't point at one thing and say that's it.
dialogue.conversations.people.again.apol: You did, aye. They've not changed since.
dialogue.conversations.people.again.pres: Twice in a day is how rumours start, %1$s.
...Fine. Still difficult. Still mine to live beside.
dialogue.conversations.people.again/1: I said my piece about the neighbors. Any more and it becomes gossip, which is a different question.
dialogue.conversations.people.again/2: Careful, %1$s — twice in a week and people start thinking YOU'RE the nosy one.
dialogue.conversations.people.again/3: Nothing's changed since you asked. Same saints, same menaces.
dialogue.conversations.people.blunt/1: ...It is my side of it. That's what a side is. But — aye. I'd not thought to say so out loud.
dialogue.conversations.people.blunt/2: Careful, %1$s. ...No, you're right. It's the version that flatters me and I know it is.
dialogue.conversations.people.blunt/3: Hm. It's easier to agree with whoever's in front of you. You didn't. I'll think about that.
dialogue.conversations.people.child/1: The miller's kid is my best friend except on race days.
dialogue.conversations.people.child/2: Everyone's nice! Except when they're telling me to slow down.
dialogue.conversations.people.defend.low: ...Perhaps. I'm in no state to be fair about them today, and you're probably right anyway.
You'd defend them. Of course you would. I'd defend them too, on a better afternoon.
Mm. Ask me tomorrow, %1$s, and I might agree with you properly.
Exhausting. You've no idea. They cross the lane when they see me coming.
It is. Though I'll grant they've their reasons, %1$s, which is the tiring part.
Just so. Try living alongside people who've decided what you are already.
dialogue.conversations.people.encourage_: ...Talk to them. Out loud. Like people. ...I've been avoiding that for two years and you said it in six words.
You're right and I hate it, %1$s. I'll go round tomorrow. Don't watch me do it.
You've not met them. Talking is what started it.
Easy to say from outside it, %1$s.
Don't. You've heard one side of it for two minutes and you're handing out remedies.
Have I tried talking to them. Yes. Remarkably, that occurred to me before you arrived.
...I could. I've thought about it. Hearing somebody else say it makes it smaller.
Talking. Aye. It's the obvious thing and the hardest one.
dialogue.conversations.people.first/1: Good folk, mostly. We share fences, weather, and opinions about each other. It works.
dialogue.conversations.people.first/2: You live close enough to anyone, you learn their sneezes by name. I know everyone's sneeze.
dialogue.conversations.people.first/3: The neighbors? We feud gently and forgive quickly. Village rules.
dialogue.conversations.people.followup.e: ...It is. Living beside people is the whole job, some weeks.
Exhausting is the word. Thank you for not telling me to be patient.
You'd think a small village would be less work. It's more.
...No. I've been avoiding it for a season. Maybe I should.
Talking. There's a thought. Everyone here prefers a grudge.
You make it sound simple. It might even be.
dialogue.conversations.people.followup.j: Ha! We would. Take away the complaining and there'd be nothing to do of an evening.
That's uncomfortably close to the truth, %1$s. I'd like it noted that I resent it.
Lost entirely. It's the one thing that keeps us all turning up to the same well.
dialogue.conversations.people.followup.p: ...No. I've said more than I meant to already.
I'll not name names to someone who asks like that, %1$s.
That's not what this was. Let it lie.
dialogue.conversations.people.fond.agree: Then you've had the proper welcome. Not everyone does.
Good. They've had practice — you're not the first stray we've adopted, %1$s.
Of course they have. It's the one thing this place is unarguably good at.
dialogue.conversations.people.fond.favou: The baker, and I'll deny it if it gets back to the miller.
That's a trap and I'm not walking into it, %1$s. ...The baker.
Whoever's least trouble that week. It rotates. Currently: nobody.
dialogue.conversations.people.fond.how_l: All my life, most of them. I watched half this village learn to walk.
Long enough to have forgiven every one of them at least twice, %1$s.
Twenty years. You stop counting and start belonging somewhere in there.
dialogue.conversations.people.fond.leave: So it is. One of them will want something within the hour.
Off you go, %1$s. Say hello to whoever you pass.
dialogue.conversations.people.fond.share: Of course you have. That's what the place is for.
Good. Then somebody did their job, and I'd like to know who so I can thank them.
You have, %1$s. I've heard three people say your name kindly this month.
dialogue.conversations.people.fond.tease: Especially those. A returned tool means nothing; a borrowed one means trust.
Ha! You've met the miller, then.
Even them, %1$s. I've a shovel out there living a whole second life.
dialogue.conversations.people.gossip.bac: ...That's the most decent thing anybody's done in this conversation.
Ha. You've saved us both, %1$s. I'd have regretted it by supper.
Right. Good. Let's talk about the weather like sensible people.
dialogue.conversations.people.gossip.dis: ...Then here it is. The miller's brother has been counting my firewood.
I'll hold you to that, %1$s. Right — you know the well? Two of them fought over it.
Good. Then you'll understand why I've stopped lending anything.
dialogue.conversations.people.judgy/1: Half of them owe me favors and the other half owe me apologies. I keep a list.
dialogue.conversations.people.judgy/2: Fine people, if you like noise, borrowed tools that never return, and opinions at dawn.
dialogue.conversations.people.judgy/3: I'd rank them, but you'd repeat it, and then I'd have to rank you too.
dialogue.conversations.people.rebuffed.c: ...That's a better answer than I deserved for that. Come back in spring.
Few people say that. Most argue harder, %1$s.
True enough. Earn one and I'll listen to it properly.
dialogue.conversations.people.rebuffed.h: Keep it, then. Quietly, if you would.
You would. Everyone does, %1$s, for about a year.
Mm. We'll see which of us is right about them.
dialogue.conversations.people.respond.ag: Then it isn't just me. That's a relief, honestly.
You've seen it too. Nobody says it out loud around here.
Quite. Good neighbours, mostly. Mostly is doing some work in that sentence.
dialogue.conversations.people.respond.as: You want the specifics. Alright — but this stays here.
One example. Just one, or we'll be here till dark.
Ha. How long have you got, %1$s?
dialogue.conversations.people.respond.de: Easy to defend people who've never crossed you.
...You're right. I'm being unfair and you said so kindly.
Somebody had to say it back to me. They're not so bad.
Fair. I'd rather be corrected than agreed with out of politeness.
They're not, mostly. I'm just tired of them this week.
True enough. Everyone's someone's difficult neighbour.
It is. I say worse than I mean.
dialogue.conversations.people.respond.le: Wise. Nothing good comes of stirring it.
So I've found. Best left alone.
Right you are. Mind who you repeat things to.
dialogue.conversations.people.resume.ask: Less than I'd planned. The planned version was a speech and speeches don't mend.
That I'd been unfair. Two words of it were true and the rest were scaffolding.
Nothing clever. 'I've been avoiding you.' That did more than a year of thinking.
dialogue.conversations.people.resume.gla: So am I, now. I was not glad at the time and I'd like that on record.
It took a fortnight of deciding and eleven minutes of doing.
Don't be too pleased. I've one conversation left and it's the harder one.
dialogue.conversations.people.resume.lea: Do. I'll say if it changes, and I'll say plainly.
Right. It's mine to carry and it's lighter for having been said out loud.
Then it's mine again. That's how it should be, and thank you for the loan.
dialogue.conversations.people.resume.no_: There isn't, and that's exactly how a season becomes four.
Kind. Wrong, but kind, and I'll take the kind part with me.
No. But there's a point where waiting becomes the answer, and I'm near it.
dialogue.conversations.people.resume.tha: You asked. People who ask get told; it isn't more complicated than that.
It costs me nothing and it seems to be worth something. I'll go on doing it.
That's the second time you've thanked me for a thing I'd have done anyway.
dialogue.conversations.people.resume/1: I spoke to them. You'll want to know it was awkward and it was worth it.
dialogue.conversations.people.resume/2: I've not spoken to them. You said I should and I've been finding reasons.
dialogue.conversations.people.resume/3: We spoke. It didn't mend anything and it stopped it getting worse, which is something.
dialogue.conversations.people.revisit/1: You asked about the neighbors once. I've warmed up on a couple of them since. Slightly.
dialogue.conversations.people.revisit/2: Been watching folk differently since we talked. Everyone's carrying something, turns out.
dialogue.conversations.people.revisit/3: Since you asked last — the miller apologized. I nearly fainted into the flour.
dialogue.conversations.people.shy/1: They're... a lot. Kind, but a lot. I like them best from my window, waving.
dialogue.conversations.people.shy/2: Everyone's lovely. I just need three days' notice and an escape route to enjoy them.
dialogue.conversations.people.shy/3: I know them all by footstep. It saves having to look up.
dialogue.conversations.people.softened.r: Just so. It's the price of living close enough to hear each other's doors.
That's a kind way to let me off, %1$s. I'll take it and behave better.
True. And they're all being hard on me somewhere, which is only fair.
dialogue.conversations.people.teen/1: They're fine. Everybody's got opinions about my hair, though.
dialogue.conversations.people.warm/1: I love them. All of them. Even the loud ones. ESPECIALLY the loud ones.
dialogue.conversations.people.warm/2: This village is one big family that argues about fences. I wouldn't trade a single one.
dialogue.conversations.people.warm/3: Every door here would open for me at midnight if I knocked. That's wealth, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.people.wry/1: A finer collection of characters was never assembled on purpose. Note: it wasn't on purpose.
dialogue.conversations.people.wry/2: The neighbors are free theater, %1$s. The matinee is the market. Bring snacks.
dialogue.conversations.people.wry/3: Decent souls. Odd hats. The correlation is real and I'm studying it.
dialogue.conversations.people.young.ask/: ...Not unkind. Just busy. It's a bit the same, though.
One person. But I'm not saying who.
dialogue.conversations.people.young.list: The baker's lad, mostly. And the dog. The dog counts.
Most people. Not the one who shouts at the well.
Nobody my age, really. That's the trouble with here.
dialogue.conversations.quest.accepted/1: You're taking on %2$s? You're a good sort, %1$s. I won't forget it.
dialogue.conversations.quest.accepted/2: %1$s, thank you. %2$s has been weighing on me.
dialogue.conversations.quest.accepted/3: Bless you, %1$s. Get %2$s sorted and I'll make it worth your while.
dialogue.conversations.quest.completed/1: That's %2$s put to bed. Thank you, %1$s — truly.
dialogue.conversations.quest.completed/2: Good and done. I owe you for %2$s, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.quest.completed/3: %2$s, finished and dusted. You've my thanks, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.quest.failed/1: Ah... %2$s didn't work out. Don't dwell on it, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.quest.failed/2: So %2$s slipped away. It happens, %1$s. Chin up.
dialogue.conversations.quest.failed/3: %1$s, %2$s went sideways. We'll manage. We always do.
dialogue.conversations.quest.in_progress: %2$s — still on it, %1$s? No rush. Well, some rush.
dialogue.conversations.quest.none/1: Nothing needs doing right now, %1$s. But I appreciate you asking.
dialogue.conversations.quest.none/2: All's handled for the moment, %1$s. Come back and I might have work.
dialogue.conversations.quest.none/3: No, %1$s, I'm caught up. Kind of you to offer, though.
dialogue.conversations.quest.offer/1: Since you ask, %1$s — aye, there's a thing or two. Let me show you what I need.
dialogue.conversations.quest.offer/2: Funny you should ask, %1$s. I do have something that wants doing.
dialogue.conversations.quest.offer/3: As it happens, %1$s, there's work if you want it. Here, take a look.
dialogue.conversations.quest.ready/1: You've done it? Let me see — %2$s, finished! Wonderful, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.quest.ready/2: Is that %2$s done already? %1$s, you're a marvel.
dialogue.conversations.quest.ready/3: Ha! %2$s, sorted. Come here, %1$s, let me thank you proper.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.again.apo: It's alright. It isn't the sort of thing that gets lighter for a second telling.
No harm, %1$s. Once a day is already more than I usually manage.
Happens. I'd sooner you forgot you asked than remembered what I answered, truthfully.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.again.lea: Aye. Catch me later in the week.
There's nothing more to say about it today.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.again.pre: Same one. There's only ever been the one, which is either lucky or very unlucky.
Twice in a day is a lot to ask of that particular subject, %1$s.
...Fine. The short version, and then we're done with it for today.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.again/1: We turned those stones over already. Let them lie a while.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.again/2: One airing per season for those, %1$s. Doctor's orders. I'm the doctor.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.again/3: Twice in a day and I'll start thinking it's the most interesting thing about me.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.close.con: ...You didn't owe me that. It does help. It helps more than the forgiving would have.
So there's two of us carrying something. That's not comfort exactly, but it's company, %1$s.
Hm. You put yours down next to mine instead of stepping over it. I noticed.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.close.lea: Aye. Go on, and thank you.
Right. Enough of that for one day.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.close.say: ...It did. Saying it out loud stops you pretending it was smaller than it was.
Every telling I've rehearsed came out kinder to me than that one did.
You noticed that. I've spent years arranging that story so it wasn't my fault, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.close.tha: Thanking me for that is an odd thing to do. ...But I'd rather odd than nothing.
You're welcome. It's the first time I've said it and not felt worse after, %1$s.
Hm. Thank you for hearing it without arranging your face.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.first/1: One or two. There was a door I didn't knock on, years ago. I still walk past it.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.first/2: I regret the things I didn't say at a funeral once. Say your things, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.first/3: I traded a friendship for pride once. Worst deal I ever made.
...You've no idea what it would cost, %1$s.
Make it right. As though I hadn't thought of that every night since.
That's a lot to say to someone who just told you the worst of themselves.
...I could. You're right, and I've been telling myself otherwise.
Blunt. Correct. That's the pair of things I needed.
Still time, you reckon. Alright. I'll think on it properly.
Maybe. Maybe it's too late for that particular door.
You might be right. I'd want to be sure before I tried.
Perhaps. I'll not decide it standing here.
...You don't. Nobody's said that. I'm not sure I believe it, but I'll keep it.
That's a generous reading of me, %1$s. I'll try to earn it.
Careful. Say that and I might start believing it.
...That's better. Absolution I'd not have trusted. This I do.
You didn't tidy it up for me. Thank you for that.
Not fine, and not alone either. I can live with that, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.forgive.c: ...You don't get to decide that. ...And yet something just came loose. I'll not pretend it didn't.
Say that again slowly, %1$s, because I want to remember exactly how it sounded.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.forgive.p: Kind. It doesn't reach the part of me that decides these things, but it's kind.
Mm. You'd say that to anybody with a long face, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.forgive.r: Don't. Absolution from somebody who wasn't there is worth exactly nothing.
You weren't in the room. You don't get to close the door on it.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.forgive.s: ...You don't. Hm. I'll keep it and see whether it holds by morning.
That's not yours to give. I'm taking it anyway.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.guarded.a: Anything that isn't behind me. The front of my life is perfectly good company.
Ask me about now. Now I've made my peace with, %1$s.
Something I'd not have to apologise for, then. That narrows it, but not to nothing.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.guarded.l: Off you go. We'll get there or we won't.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.guarded.p: You're asking me to lift a stone I put down on purpose. Leave it where it is.
That door stays shut, %1$s, and it isn't shut because I forgot about it.
No. Some things you tell people once they've seen you at your worst and stayed. Not before.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.guarded.r: ...Thank you. It isn't a thing that improves with an audience.
So it is. You'll get it the day I can say it without my voice doing that, %1$s.
Good. Not everything wants digging up to be looked at.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.no_words/: ...Then say nothing. Everyone who has something ready has usually not listened.
Good. The people with the quick answers are the ones I stopped telling, %1$s.
That's the right amount to say. I'd been braced for advice.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.rebuked.a: ...Nearly everyone is. Few of them admit it standing there.
True enough. And now you've said it, I mind it less, %1$s.
Then we're square, and the rest of it stays where it is.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.rebuked.e: ...Then ask about the person and not the deed. That's the door.
Understanding I'll give you. The details are for the person I did it to, %1$s.
Badly asked, aye. But asked. I'll take that over the polite silence.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.rebuked.l: Good. That's the whole of what I wanted.
Right. Thank you for hearing the no.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.respond.a: ...Maybe. I've not let myself look at that question properly.
Put right. Huh. Everyone else asks what happened, not what's left.
There might be. It'd take more courage than I've had lately.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.respond.l: So it is. Thank you for not making a face about it.
Go on, %1$s. It'll still be mine tomorrow.
Right. Enough of that for one day.
...Alright. Nobody stays for this part. They remember an errand.
You'll stand there and hear it. That's the whole of what I wanted.
Then I'll say the rest, and you can decide what you think of me after.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.respond.p: Exactly what I did is mine. That I regret it is what I gave you.
You want the detail more than the person. I've noticed that before.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.resume.as: It has, a little. You told me I wasn't a bad person and it stuck.
Easier, aye. Somebody deciding I was worth forgiving did that.
Since you said what you said — yes. Odd how much a sentence weighs.
A little. You didn't tell me it was fine, and that's why I believed the rest.
Easier. Not lighter — easier. There's a difference and you knew it.
You sat with it instead of fixing it. That's what let it settle.
A little. Time does some of it. Being asked after does the rest.
Some days. It's the sort of thing that goes quiet rather than goes away.
Easier than it was, %1$s. I'd not have noticed if you hadn't asked.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.resume.br: ...You said you'd not use it against me.
That was told to you, %1$s. Not handed over.
I regret telling you more than I regret the thing, just now.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.resume.en: ...I have, since you asked last. Thinking's most of the way there.
You're going to keep asking, aren't you. Good. I need someone to.
A little. It's closer to a plan than it was, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.resume.fo: Enough. Who decides that, though? ...You, apparently. Alright. I'll try it your way.
I've been paying by instalments for years. Somebody calling it settled is a strange feeling.
That's not yours to say, %1$s. ...Say it again anyway.
No. It isn't. Plenty take the forgiving job just to end the conversation — you didn't.
That's honest, and it leaves the thing where it belongs. I respect it and I don't enjoy it.
You're right, %1$s. It's theirs. I'd been hoping you'd hand it over cheap.
True enough. Leave it be. It's good at waiting.
Right you are. Off you go.
Go on, %1$s. Thank you for not making a meal of it.
What it'd look like. Aye — that's the question I've been walking around for a long while.
Knocking on a door, mostly. It's a very short list and a very heavy one.
Saying it to the right person instead of to you. ...No offence meant. You've been good practice.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.resume.le: Quite. Best left where it is.
Thank you, %1$s. For coming back and for stopping.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.revisit/1: That thing I told you about. It's still there, mostly.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.revisit/2: I've been turning it over since we spoke. Not to much effect.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.revisit/3: You know the one. I don't need to name it twice.
dialogue.conversations.regrets.sit_with_: ...Right. Thank you. Most of the way through that I was waiting for the sound of you leaving.
You are, aren't you. ...Give me a moment and then I'll say the rest of it, %1$s.
Still here. Aye. That's the whole of what I needed and I couldn't have asked for it.
...Aye. That's kind too, in its way. Go on.
Room. Right. I'll take the room, %1$s, and thank you for not dressing it up.
Fair enough. It's a lot to put on somebody's afternoon.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.about_play: I will, and I'll be believed, which is worth more than you defending yourself.
I'll say what I've seen. That's all I can honestly do and it usually holds.
It is. It's slower than you'd like and it works better than shouting.
You will. Most of it dies on its own.
So I've found. That's the way.
You'd rather know than be the last to. I'd want the same.
It's easier to say it than to watch you not know it. Barely.
Somebody had to. I'd sooner it was me than someone enjoying it.
Careful. Half the things I know, I know because nobody checked them either.
You want it verified? That's not how any of this works, %1$s. It's a market, not a ledger.
Ask for proof and people stop telling you things. That's a worse trade than being wrong sometimes.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.doubt.hold: ...You're right, and I've been telling it all week without asking myself that.
I'll hold it, then, and see whether it turns up from anybody else.
That's the sensible line. It's also the one nobody here draws.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.doubt.who_: The people in it, and they've said nothing, which tells you something.
Nobody I'd trust twice. That's why I said it the way I said it.
The trader, if it came in on the road. Ask before he goes.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.followup.e: I'd rather not add to it. And now I wish I'd said nothing.
You want the list. That tells me something about you.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.followup.l: So it is. Best forgotten. I'll try to.
You're right. It doesn't deserve the air.
Good. Let it die at this well and not the next.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.followup.p: ...Thank you. That's not nothing, around here.
It stops with you. Good. I'd rather it had stopped with me.
I'll hold you to that, %1$s. People here rarely mean it.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.harmless.g: So am I. We've had a year of worse and this makes a pleasant change.
True enough. Small news is the sign of a village that's doing well.
Careful. Say that too loudly and something worse turns up out of spite.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.harmless.w: Because a village that only speaks about serious things stops speaking.
Fair. I'd say it's how we keep track of each other, but you're not wrong.
Habit, mostly. You've made me hear it, which I'll be cross about later.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.more.anyth: Some. Not unkind, exactly — people wonder where you go and they say so.
There is. Somebody thinks you're too free with what you find, and said it loudly.
None at all, and that's worth knowing. You're not interesting enough to invent.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.more.do_yo: Half. The shape of it, yes. The details have grown legs since I first heard it.
No. I've told you because you asked, not because I'd swear to it.
I did until you asked me plainly. Now I find I'd rather not answer.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.more.is_it: No. It's the sort of thing we say when there's nothing to say.
Not remotely. Nobody's hurt by it, which is my whole test for these things.
Less than it sounded. I told it with more weight than it deserves.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.more.is_th: A season, near enough. You're the last person here to hear it.
New this week, which is why it's still being said with any energy.
Old enough that I'd forgotten it and then someone started it up again.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.more/1: Ask me about it properly and you'll get a straighter answer than the telling was.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.more/2: There's what's said and there's what I think. Ask, and you can have the second.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.more/3: Go on. I'd rather be questioned about it than quoted on it.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.none.ask_a: Nothing worth your time. And I'd tell you if there were.
Not a whisper. Come back after market day.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.none.relie: It does me too. Quiet weeks are underrated.
So I've found. Nothing to repeat means nothing went wrong.
Good. Long may it stay dull, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.none/1: Rumors? It's been dead quiet, %1$s. Not so much as a misplaced goat to talk about.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.none/2: Nothing's going round just now. Give the village a week — there's always something eventually.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.none/3: No fresh talk that I've heard. And I'd have heard it, believe me. These walls are thin.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.private.as: ...Them. Not the story. No one has asked that, and I've told four people this week.
Badly, and privately, and they'd not want it discussed. Thank you for asking anyway.
That's the right question. I'll tell them somebody asked it, without saying who.
It's the kind you'd hear anyway. I'd rather you heard it without the trimmings.
It's the kind that changes how you'd speak to somebody. That's why I said anything.
It's the kind people are careful about. Now you know to be careful too.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.private.le: Right. Then we're agreed and neither of us has to mention it again.
Good. Off you go, and thank you.
Fine. That's the end of it, which is where I wanted it.
...Thank you. Everyone wants the rest and I've had to say no all week.
You'll leave it. Right. That's the first time anybody has this fortnight.
Then it stays where it is. I'll not forget that you let it.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.private.pr: No. It's a death in somebody's family, not a story for the square.
That's exactly why I didn't say. Ask the family or don't ask.
I said as much as I'm willing to. That was the sentence and I meant it.
Good. That's the whole of what I wanted out of telling you.
Then I was right about you, which I'd been about eighty per cent sure of.
Thank you. I'll know by Thursday whether that was true, and I expect it will be.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.respond.as: ...Fair question. Second-hand, if I'm honest. Maybe third.
Nobody ever asks that. Which is rather how these things spread.
The well, where else. Which means it's half invented already.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.respond.ch: ...No. It doesn't, does it. I repeated it without thinking.
You're right to doubt it. I doubted it and said it anyway.
Reliable's a strong word for anything said near that well.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.respond.le: Just so. I shouldn't have started.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.respond.li: Right. Well. There's not much more, when I say it aloud.
That's most of it. It sounded bigger in my head.
You're an easy person to tell things to. Dangerous, that.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.resume.bel: ...Thank you. I'd worked out what I'd say if you didn't, and I'd rather not use it.
That's worth more than you'd think in a village this size.
Good. Because the alternative was me proving a negative all winter.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.resume.lea: Do. I'll say if it changes, and I'll say plainly.
Right. It's mine to carry and it's lighter for having been said out loud.
Then it's mine again. That's how it should be, and thank you for the loan.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.resume.let: It will, if neither of us feeds it. That's the whole of how these things end.
Agreed. Three weeks of silence and it's a thing that used to be said.
That's the plan. Ask me in a season whether it worked.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.resume.tha: You asked. People who ask get told; it isn't more complicated than that.
It costs me nothing and it seems to be worth something. I'll go on doing it.
That's the second time you've thanked me for a thing I'd have done anyway.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.resume.who: I've a guess and I'll not say it, because a guess said aloud becomes a second rumour.
Three people knew. I'll leave the arithmetic to you and not do it out loud.
That's the question that turns one problem into two. I've decided not to ask it.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.resume/1: That thing I said I'd keep. I've kept it, and it has been harder than I expected.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.resume/2: It got out. Not through me, and I'd like you to believe that, which is a thing I can't prove.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.resume/3: Nobody's mentioned it in three weeks. That's what a thing dying looks like.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.stale.die/: It would have, if people stopped feeding it. That includes me, I know.
It's trying to. Every retelling gives it another fortnight.
So it is. I'll not be the one who carries it into next season.
dialogue.conversations.rumors.stale.unto: That's how you know where you stand here. It takes a year to be told first.
They will next time. Being told late is the last stage before being told early.
I assumed somebody had. That's what everyone assumes, and so nobody does.
dialogue.conversations.season.again/1: We did the seasons already. The wheel hasn't turned since breakfast.
dialogue.conversations.season.again/2: Same time of year as when you last asked, %1$s. It moves slower than you do.
dialogue.conversations.season.again/3: Ask me again at the turn and I'll have something new. Not before.
dialogue.conversations.season.agree.pass: Suppose so. It turns whether I notice it or not, which is rather restful.
It comes round. It always comes round. There's a comfort in the ordinariness of it, %1$s.
Quite. Nothing much to say about it, and that's rather the point of a good season.
dialogue.conversations.season.any/1: Season's turning like it always does. I just keep pace with it and try not to grumble too loud.
dialogue.conversations.season.any/2: Oh, the year rolls on, %1$s. Some days I mark it, most days the work does the marking for me.
dialogue.conversations.season.any/3: Same wheel it always is — sun, rain, harvest, frost. Comforting to know what's coming, I find.
dialogue.conversations.season.ask_favour: Favourite? None of them, particularly. It's just the ordinary middle of the year.
There's no festival to point at, %1$s. Just the days going by, which suits me.
The ones with nothing happening in them. Those are underrated.
dialogue.conversations.season.autumn/1: Autumn already. The leaves are going gold and I've the harvest and the woodpile both on my mind.
dialogue.conversations.season.autumn/2: There's a bite in the mornings now. Time to lay stores by before winter comes knocking, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.season.autumn/3: I love the fall, honestly. Everything ripe at once, then the quiet after. Bittersweet, that.
dialogue.conversations.season.holiday.ac: ...I will. That's the first time anyone's asked to be counted in.
A place saved, then. Don't be late — the good bread goes early.
Done. And you'll be introduced to everyone, so brace yourself, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.season.holiday.as: Same as we always have. Garlands, too much food, and someone crying by midnight.
The old way, mostly. My mother's way, if I'm honest, and hers before that.
You stand in the square until someone hands you a drink. It's a robust tradition.
dialogue.conversations.season.holiday.co: We do, don't we. One day a season where nobody's counting the cost.
It's the one thing this village agrees on. Enjoy it while it lasts.
Kind of you to say. We work at it more than we let on.
dialogue.conversations.season.holiday.de: Fair enough. It'll come round again — they always do.
Another year, then. I'll save you a story instead of a seat.
No matter. It's the asking that counts more than the coming.
dialogue.conversations.season.holiday.gr: ...It's the one good day, %1$s. Let us have it.
Fuss is the point. That's what a festival is.
Mm. You needn't come, you know.
It IS. Someone had to say it. Garlands don't hang themselves.
Ha! Every year I swear I'll do less and every year there's more.
A great deal of fuss for one evening. Worth it. Barely.
Just so, but the alternative is an ordinary Tuesday.
A fair bit, yes. Somebody has to do the hanging.
dialogue.conversations.season.holiday.ha: Harvest festival! Barns full, tables fuller. Sit with us tonight, %1$s — nobody eats alone this evening.
It's harvest home. A year's work's in the store at last, and we thank the fields the only way we know — a feast.
Best day of the autumn, this. The harvest's in, the ale's out, and even I'll crack a smile before the night's done.
dialogue.conversations.season.holiday.le: Aye — there's a great deal to do before dusk.
Go on. Come by the square later if you change your mind.
Right you are. Happy day to you, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.season.holiday.mi: Midsummer! Longest day of the year — there'll be a bonfire in the square tonight, and I'll not miss it.
It's the midsummer feast, %1$s. Dance till the short dark and sleep it off tomorrow. That's the tradition.
Feel that sun? Midsummer's come round again. We light the fires at dusk to keep the light a little longer.
Midwinter's night — the year's darkest. We light every candle we've got and dare the dark to outlast us.
It's midwinter, %1$s. Cold and long, but the whole village gathers close and shares what little warmth there is.
Deep midwinter. We tell the old stories tonight and toast to the light coming back. It always does, in the end.
dialogue.conversations.season.holiday.sh: Did you? Tell me — I collect other people's versions of this day.
Everywhere does it slightly wrong except here, obviously. Go on, though.
That's the good thing about the festivals. Everyone brings their own.
dialogue.conversations.season.holiday.sp: You picked the spring bloom to visit! The whole village is out with flowers in their hair. Even I've got a sprig.
It's the bloom, %1$s — first flowers of the year. We hang garlands and pretend winter never happened.
Spring bloom today! The children have been weaving crowns since dawn. Try one on, you've earned it.
dialogue.conversations.season.spring/1: Spring suits me. Everything's waking up — green on the fields, lambs in the pen, mud on every doorstep.
dialogue.conversations.season.spring/2: You can smell the thaw, %1$s. I've seeds to get in the ground and I'll not waste a day of it.
dialogue.conversations.season.spring/3: New season, new start. The birds are back and so's my good mood, near enough.
dialogue.conversations.season.summer/1: High summer — long days, short tempers by the forge, and cold well-water that's worth its weight in gold.
dialogue.conversations.season.summer/2: Warm enough to work till the light's gone. I'll be glad of the shade come noon, mind.
dialogue.conversations.season.summer/3: The summer's good to us, %1$s. Crops standing tall and the market full. Make the most of it before the turn.
dialogue.conversations.season.toddler.as: Everything! But mostly the smell. It smells different.
You get to do the thing! You know. The thing.
The food's better and nobody makes me go to bed on time.
dialogue.conversations.season.toddler.le: See you when it's the next one!
dialogue.conversations.season.toddler/1: I like the season where the flowers come. Is it that one?
dialogue.conversations.season.toddler/2: Leaves! There are SO many leaves.
dialogue.conversations.season.toddler/3: Every day is puddle season if you believe.
dialogue.conversations.season.turn.agree: Does it? Huh. I'll take it. That's the first useful thing anyone's said about the weather.
It's the one I complain about least, so probably.
True enough, maybe. Something about it fits the way I work.
dialogue.conversations.season.turn.ask_f: The one just turning, usually. I'm easily persuaded by a change.
Autumn. Everything ripe at once and then the quiet after.
Whichever one isn't currently happening, if I'm honest.
dialogue.conversations.season.turn.compl: There's good in it if you look. I'd rather look.
Mm. Wishing a season away wishes the year away with it.
Aye! It goes on too long every single year and nobody admits it.
Thank you. Everyone else is being relentlessly cheerful about it.
Right there with you. Roll on the next one.
You and everyone. It'll turn soon enough.
It has its moments. Few of them, but it has them.
So it is, it drags. They all do by the end.
dialogue.conversations.season.turn.dismi: All the same. Right. I'll spare you the rest of my thoughts on it.
Mm. It isn't, but I'll not argue about weather.
dialogue.conversations.season.turn.leave: Quite, the light goes early this time of year. Off you go.
Right you are. Mind the road, %1$s.
Go on. The year'll still be turning tomorrow.
dialogue.conversations.season.turn.look_: There is, when you list it out like that. I forget to.
True enough. I'd stopped counting the good things. Thanks for the reminder.
You're a more hopeful sort than I am, %1$s. It's catching.
dialogue.conversations.season.turn.share: Oh, tell me — I like knowing what people do with a season.
That's more of a plan than I've got. Mine is 'keep up'.
Good. A season with a plan in it goes faster and hurts less.
dialogue.conversations.season.winter/1: Winter's here, and it doesn't ask permission. I keep the fire fed and my complaints to myself. Mostly.
dialogue.conversations.season.winter/2: Cold enough to crack stone, %1$s. Wrap up out there — the road ices over past the well.
dialogue.conversations.season.winter/3: We hunker down this time of year. Stew on the pot, snow on the sill, and a long wait for green.
dialogue.conversations.secret.again.apol: It's alright. It's not the sort of thing that improves by repetition.
No harm, %1$s. Ask me in a few days.
Happens. I lose track of what I've said to whom, too.
dialogue.conversations.secret.again.leav: Aye. Catch me later in the week.
dialogue.conversations.secret.again.pres: Same answer, and quieter this time, because the walls haven't moved either.
One a season, I said. Asking twice in a day is how people end up with nothing, %1$s.
...Fine. But you're getting the small one, and you're not getting another for a while.
dialogue.conversations.secret.again/1: One secret per season, %1$s. Any faster and they stop being secrets.
dialogue.conversations.secret.again/2: You've had your secret. I'm still nervous about the last one.
dialogue.conversations.secret.again/3: Greedy! Secrets need time to grow back, like carrots. Dark, private carrots.
dialogue.conversations.secret.close.conf: ...You'd trade. Right. Now we've each got a rope round the other's ankle, and that's how it should be.
Secrets are traded, not given — I've said that to people for years and nobody ever took me up on it, %1$s.
Go on, then. Quietly. ...There. Now neither of us can talk.
dialogue.conversations.secret.close.leav: Aye. Go on, and thank you.
Right. Enough of that for one day.
dialogue.conversations.secret.close.say_: ...It did. More than I'd admit standing here.
Saying it out loud was the hard part. You made it easier.
dialogue.conversations.secret.close.than: You don't have to thank me for it. ...But thank you for the thanking.
It's not a gift, %1$s. Still — aye. You're welcome.
Strange thing to be thanked for. I'll take it.
dialogue.conversations.secret.declined.c: Gladly. Ask me about the fence, the weather, anything with no weight to it.
Something easier. Aye, let's. My head's had enough of the hard thing for one day.
Right you are. Easier things it is, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.secret.declined.l: Off you go. It'll be here, unfortunately.
Go on. I'll get back to pretending there's nothing to say.
dialogue.conversations.secret.declined.o: ...When I'm ready. That's a door left open, not a hand pulling at it. I'll remember which you chose.
You'll be about. Aye. That's worth more to me than the telling would have been, %1$s.
Then I'll know where to find you when it gets too big to hold. That's a comfort, oddly.
dialogue.conversations.secret.first/1: There's a thing I've never said out loud in this village. I can hand it to you now, or we can talk about the weather and both pretend I never offered.
dialogue.conversations.secret.first/2: Come closer. ...No. I'll say it properly or not at all. Do you want the thing I've been carrying about, %1$s, or shall we leave it where it is?
dialogue.conversations.secret.first/3: I've got one. A real one — the kind you don't get back once it's out in the air. Say the word and it's yours.
dialogue.conversations.secret.followup.n: ...You won't promise. That's more honest than a promise, in truth.
Trying is what people actually do. Promising is what they say.
I'd rather have your 'I'll try' than someone else's oath, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.secret.followup.p: ...I never doubted it. I asked because saying it out loud makes it a thing between us.
Your word. I'd already have staked the whole thing on it, %1$s, but it's good to hear.
Then it's safe, and I knew it was before I opened my mouth. That's why I opened my mouth.
...Your word. Then I'll sleep tonight for the first time in a while.
I'm holding you to that, %1$s. It's the only thing I've asked of you.
Good. Then it's two of us and no more, ever.
dialogue.conversations.secret.followup.t: I've carried that for eleven years, %1$s, and you weighed it in a breath.
Forget I said it. Truly — forget it.
dialogue.conversations.secret.guarded.as: Now that I can do. Ask me anything that isn't underneath.
Something lighter. Aye — we'll build up to the rest.
dialogue.conversations.secret.guarded.le: Off you go. We'll get there or we won't.
dialogue.conversations.secret.guarded.pr: I could. I'm choosing not to. There's a difference.
Pushing at that door tells me more about you than it opens, %1$s.
No. Not for the asking, and not for asking twice.
dialogue.conversations.secret.guarded.re: ...Thank you. People usually take a 'not yet' as a challenge.
It is. Ask me again when we've more winters between us, %1$s.
Good. That's how it stays worth telling later.
dialogue.conversations.secret.respond.ac: ...Alright. The 'famous' pie I bring to every festival? The trader sells it to me. Every year. I've been thanked for it eleven times.
You said that without hesitating. That's why it's you. ...I have never once liked the mayor's speeches. I clap because the baker watches.
Right. Once it's out it's out. ...There's a loose brick behind the well. My rainy-day emeralds live under it. Now two of us know where.
dialogue.conversations.secret.respond.as: Because you've never repeated a thing I've said. I've been counting. ...So: the festival pie. I buy it from the trader. I have never baked one in my life.
Because you asked why instead of leaning in. That's the answer, %1$s. ...And the answer to the other question is that I clap at the mayor to keep the baker happy.
Because there's nobody else. Less flattering, but honest. ...Loose brick, behind the well. Everything I've saved is under it. That's the thing.
dialogue.conversations.secret.respond.de: ...That's a kind thing to say to someone about to make a mistake. Right. It stays in, then.
You'd turn it down to protect me from myself. Noted, %1$s. ...It keeps. It's kept this long.
Mm. Perhaps you're right. It's waited years; it can wait a while longer.
dialogue.conversations.secret.respond.le: So I've found. Perhaps that's wiser.
Off you go. I'll not hold it against you.
dialogue.conversations.secret.resume.ask: Nobody. You're the whole list, %1$s. That's why I check the door when I say it.
Not a soul. I've had chances — I've had drink and company and chances — and no.
Just you. Which means if it ever gets out, I'll know exactly where to look. ...That's not a threat. It's just arithmetic.
dialogue.conversations.secret.resume.che: ...You asked after me, not the secret. You always were the right person to tell.
Lighter, since you know. That's the whole use of having told someone, %1$s.
Better. Knowing one person carries it with me changes the weight of it.
...You asked after ME, not the secret. Nobody does that.
Lighter, since somebody else knows. That's the whole use of telling.
Some days it's heavy. Today, less so, because you asked.
dialogue.conversations.secret.resume.fol: Lighter than it was. Heavy things don't stop being heavy; they just get better handles.
Some weeks. Not this one. You asking is part of why not this one, %1$s.
It is. But it's a shared heavy now, and that's a completely different weight.
Just so. Off you go, and thank you for the checking.
Go on, %1$s. I sleep better for these little conversations.
If it gets out... I'd know it wasn't you, first. Then I'd survive it. I've worked that far.
I'd deny it once, badly, and then I'd stop denying it. That's as far as the plan goes.
Hm. ...It would be a bad week, and then it would be a Tuesday, I expect. Ask me something easier.
I know. I check anyway — not on you, on the world. It's a habit, not a doubt.
Says the only person who could break it. ...And hasn't. That's the whole of my evidence, %1$s.
Safe. Right. I'll put that sentence somewhere I can get at it on the bad nights.
dialogue.conversations.secret.resume.hin: ...Say that again and I'll know exactly what you are.
You're joking. Tell me you're joking, %1$s.
That is the one thing. The ONE thing I asked.
dialogue.conversations.secret.resume.lea: So it is. Thank you for saying so out loud.
Off you go, %1$s. And thank you.
Right you are. It's safe. I know.
dialogue.conversations.secret.resume.ref: You wouldn't promise, and you've kept it anyway. That says more.
No oath from you. And still not a word out. I think about that.
You only said you'd try. You tried, %1$s. That'll do.
You gave your word and you've kept it. I checked, in my way. Thank you.
Nobody's looked at me strangely since. That's how I know, %1$s.
A promise kept. It's rarer than you'd think, and I noticed.
It's still between us, then. Good.
Nobody's mentioned it. I take that as an answer.
Still ours. That's all I wanted to know.
dialogue.conversations.secret.revisit/1: Still keeping what I told you? ...Good. Then maybe there's another where that came from, someday.
dialogue.conversations.secret.revisit/2: You never breathed a word about last time. I noticed. I don't forget that kind of quiet.
dialogue.conversations.secret.revisit/3: Since you kept the last one — there's a second thing, same shape as the first. That's all I'm saying today.
dialogue.conversations.secret.slighted.a: ...No. It wasn't. Thank you for turning round and saying so.
It took me nine years to say it and you nine words to file it, %1$s. But — alright.
Then we'll leave it where it landed and I'll not take it back.
dialogue.conversations.secret.slighted.s: ...That's the part that mattered anyway. Keep it, then.
Safe. Aye. That's more use than impressed, if I'm honest, %1$s.
Then it wasn't wasted. Which is what I was actually afraid of.
dialogue.conversations.standing.again.ap: No harm. It's a thing worth worrying at, I'll grant you.
You have a lot on your mind, %1$s. So does everyone here.
Quite. Come back tomorrow and I might have something new.
dialogue.conversations.standing.again.pr: Same as this morning: it moves slower than you'd like and faster than you'd think.
Nothing's shifted, %1$s. That in itself is worth knowing.
Ask the village, not me. They'll tell you the same twice too.
dialogue.conversations.standing.again/1: Asking again? Standing doesn't shift by the hour, %1$s. But go on.
dialogue.conversations.standing.again/2: Same as when you last asked, more or less. Reputations move slowly here.
dialogue.conversations.standing.again/3: Still taking the village's temperature, %1$s? All right, once more.
dialogue.conversations.standing.amends.d: Saying it where people can hear — that's a start, %1$s. I'll make sure it's known you said it.
That took something. Words don't undo it, but they open the door. Folk will hear of this.
All right. An apology, given in the open. It won't settle everything, %1$s, but it counts.
dialogue.conversations.standing.bad.back: So I've found. What else, then?
dialogue.conversations.standing.bad.deed: Well — %2$s. That's the one that comes up.
The thing people mention? %2$s. Make of that what you will.
It's %2$s they talk about, when your name comes up.
dialogue.conversations.standing.bad.dism: Suit yourself, %1$s. But a village's memory is longer than its patience.
If you say so. The people whose opinions 'don't matter' are the ones you'll trade with tomorrow.
Mm. You asked, mind. Don't ask if you don't want to hear it.
dialogue.conversations.standing.bad.foll: Do that. It's worth thinking on.
A lecture, was it? Then I'll save my breath next time.
You asked, %1$s. Snapping at the answer is a fine way to prove the talk right.
As you like. Don't come asking again if the answer stings.
You took that better than most. It'll be remembered kindly, %1$s.
Straight talk deserves straight thanks. That's a start, that is.
That's all anyone can do — hear it and carry on.
dialogue.conversations.standing.bad.mend: Time and a dozen small kindnesses nobody thanks you for. There's no shortcut.
Be useful where it costs you something, %1$s. People can tell the difference.
Stop giving them new material. That alone would do half of it.
dialogue.conversations.standing.bad.prot: Maybe not. A village judges what it sees, not what you are.
I've thought that myself about my own name, %1$s. It changed nothing until I did.
Then you've the harder job: being the other thing where people are looking.
dialogue.conversations.standing.bad/1: You'd hear it kindlier from me than most: %2$s is the word for you here, and it wasn't given lightly.
dialogue.conversations.standing.bad/2: Honestly? Doors don't open easily for you, %1$s. %2$s, they say. That takes mending, not waiting.
dialogue.conversations.standing.bad/3: People keep their distance, and you know why. %2$s — that's how you're spoken of.
dialogue.conversations.standing.child/1: People talk about grown-up things like that. I just know if you're nice or not.
dialogue.conversations.standing.child/2: Mama says it's rude to repeat what people say. But nobody's thrown anything at you!
dialogue.conversations.standing.good.bac: So it is. What else, then?
dialogue.conversations.standing.good.dee: Well — %2$s. That's the one that comes up.
The thing people mention? %2$s. It's done you no harm at all.
It's %2$s they talk about, and they talk about it kindly.
dialogue.conversations.standing.good.def: No. The ones who would say it are rarely the ones we mean it about.
That's rather the point of it being other people's opinion, %1$s.
Then it's a good thing you're not the one keeping the tally.
dialogue.conversations.standing.good.dis: Suit yourself, %1$s. Though it's a strange thing to shrug off.
If you say so. It's the only inheritance most people here get.
dialogue.conversations.standing.good.fol: That's the only way it's ever held, %1$s. Nobody coasts here.
Say that where the others can hear and you'll have half the village.
Good. A name's a loan, not a gift.
Straight talk deserves straight thanks. We'll get along, %1$s.
You took that as well as you took the bad news you've never had from me.
That's all anyone can do — hear it and carry on.
dialogue.conversations.standing.good.kee: Turning up. That's most of it, %1$s — turning up when it's inconvenient.
Not spending it. A good name goes fastest when its owner starts leaning on it.
Being the same person in the square as you are on the road.
dialogue.conversations.standing.good/1: You're well thought of, %1$s. %2$s, people say, and they say it warmly.
dialogue.conversations.standing.good/2: Around here? %2$s. You've earned that — folk notice what you do.
dialogue.conversations.standing.good/3: Good things, mostly. %2$s is how they put it, and nobody argues.
dialogue.conversations.standing.incident: Fair enough.
Quite. What else, then?
I'll see you about, %1$s.
%2$s. That's the matter, and nobody's called it settled.
It's %2$s, %1$s. You'll not have needed me to tell you.
The word on it is %2$s. Said quietly, but said often.
It rarely is. That's never yet stopped a village from settling on a version.
Then say so where they can hear it, %1$s. Telling me changes nothing.
Possibly. But nobody's asked for your telling of it, and that's the trouble.
Suit yourself, %1$s. But a village's memory is longer than its patience.
If you say so. It'll be waiting for you the next time you need a favour.
Mm. You asked, mind. Don't ask if you don't want to hear it.
Do that. There's time yet.
It is. Off you go, %1$s.
Away you go.
A lecture, was it? Then I'll save my breath next time.
You asked, %1$s. Snapping at the answer is a fine way to prove the talk right.
As you like. Don't come asking again if the answer stings.
You took that better than most. It'll be remembered kindly, %1$s.
Somebody had to say it to your face. I'd rather it were me than the crowd.
That's all anyone can do — hear it and carry on.
dialogue.conversations.standing.mixed.di: They do. And you'll go on wondering which half you're speaking to.
That half buys bread from the same baker you do. Think on it.
Then I've told you for nothing, and I'll keep the next one to myself.
dialogue.conversations.standing.mixed.fo: That's why I gave you both. A comfortable answer would have cost you a year.
Then you'll get the truth from me every time, which not everybody wants.
Good. The ones who only want the warm half never mend anything, %1$s.
That's the work, and it's slow. Years, not weeks, and no thanks along the way.
Then start with the ones who won't look at you. The rest follow them.
It can be done. I've watched it done twice here and both took patience.
dialogue.conversations.standing.mixed.le: They will, with or without your permission. It's the village's favourite pastime.
That's healthier than begging either half, I'll say that for it.
Careful. Left alone, an argument settles on whichever side talks loudest.
dialogue.conversations.standing.mixed.wh: The one bad day. It's the one they tell, because it's the one with a shape to it.
Nothing you could fix by asking. They want to see a second year of you, not hear about the first.
That you arrived and things changed. Some people can't tell those two apart.
The forgiving one, though I got there later than I'd like to admit.
Neither, honestly. I've been waiting to see which way you go before I pick.
Yours, %1$s. That's why you're getting this instead of a polite nothing.
dialogue.conversations.standing.mixed/1: You'll get two answers depending who you ask, %1$s. Half the village has let it go and half hasn't.
dialogue.conversations.standing.mixed/2: It isn't one thing. Some here think well of you and some are still carrying what happened.
dialogue.conversations.standing.mixed/3: Split, if I'm honest with you. You've done enough good that it gets argued about, which is rare.
Fair enough.
So it is. What else, then?
Take care of yourself, %1$s.
Suit yourself. Though 'nobody' is a hard name to trade under.
If you say so. It'll matter the first time you need something, %1$s.
Mm. You asked, mind.
Do that.
True enough. Off you go, %1$s.
Safe home.
That's the spirit of it. Start small and start where it's seen.
Careful what, mind. They'll say something either way, %1$s.
Good. Nothing wins a village like being useful twice running.
It's not much of a verdict to be thanked for, but you're welcome.
Straight's all I've got, %1$s. Glad it was useful.
Ask me again in a season and there'll be more to say.
Be seen doing something dull and necessary. That's how everyone here started.
Help one person publicly, %1$s. The village does the rest of the arithmetic.
Show up twice for the same thing. Twice is what makes it a habit in people's mouths.
Me? You ask questions nobody else asks. I've not decided if that's good yet.
I'd say you're easier to talk to than most who pass through, %1$s. Take that as you like.
I've an opinion. It isn't the village's, and I'll keep it a while longer.
It does have its comforts. Nobody expects anything of a stranger.
Plenty here would trade with you for that, %1$s. Reputation is mostly weight.
Then you've the rarest thing in a village: a clean start you can keep.
dialogue.conversations.standing.neutral/: Truthfully? Most people don't know you well enough to have an opinion yet, %1$s.
You're a face people are still placing. Neither warm nor cold — just new.
Nothing bad, nothing much at all yet. Give it time and give them reasons.
dialogue.conversations.standing.no_tally: Nobody keeps a tally here, %1$s. There's no ledger to look you up in.
I couldn't tell you how the village reads you. We've never been a place that counts.
Standing? We haven't a word for it here. People have opinions and they keep them indoors.
dialogue.conversations.standing.praise.a: It is. We're none of us built to hear ourselves described kindly.
Quite. Take a moment with it — you don't have to have an answer ready.
Odd and good at once. Sit in it a while before you argue with it.
dialogue.conversations.standing.praise.d: Not here they won't. It took something out of them to say it.
Then I've wasted a kindness on you, and I'll not make that mistake twice.
They said it about you when you weren't stood there. That's the one kind that counts.
dialogue.conversations.standing.praise.f: Somebody should. Kind words die in the street if nobody carries them.
It cost me nothing and it seems to have been worth something. Good trade.
I'd want it done for me, %1$s, so I do it for other people.
dialogue.conversations.standing.praise.w: That %2$s was the sort of thing they'd not have thought to do themselves.
They brought up %2$s, and then they said your name the way you say a neighbour's.
%2$s came up. What stuck with me is that nobody argued with them.
I'll not name them. They said it freely because they thought it stayed here.
Somebody who'd deny it if you asked. That's how you know they meant it.
More than one, which is why I bothered to mention it at all.
dialogue.conversations.standing.praise/1: Someone spoke well of you where you couldn't hear it, %1$s. I thought you ought to know it happened.
dialogue.conversations.standing.praise/2: You came up in conversation this week, and not one unkind word in it.
dialogue.conversations.standing.praise/3: I'll pass this on because nobody else will: people say good things about you when you're absent.
dialogue.conversations.standing.resume.k: Do. And don't perform it — performed decency is worse than none in a village.
Right. Another year and it'll be one answer, and nobody will remember it wasn't.
Good. I'll keep watching, which is the only useful thing I do.
dialogue.conversations.standing.resume.l: Do. I'll say if it changes, and I'll say plainly.
Right. It's mine to carry and it's lighter for having been said out loud.
Then it's mine again. That's how it should be, and thank you for the loan.
dialogue.conversations.standing.resume.t: You asked. People who ask get told; it isn't more complicated than that.
It costs me nothing and it seems to be worth something. I'll go on doing it.
That's the second time you've thanked me for a thing I'd have done anyway.
I'd be tired too. That doesn't stop them measuring, and it doesn't stop me telling you.
Then stop asking me and it stops. That's a real option and I'd not think less of you.
Fair. I'd say give it one more season, and I'd say that whatever you answered.
dialogue.conversations.standing.resume.w: The baker, and she'll deny it. That's how you know it's a real change.
Two of the ones who were loudest. Loud opinions turn over faster than quiet ones.
I'll not name them. Naming them would make it a scoreboard and it isn't one.
dialogue.conversations.standing.resume/1: You said you'd keep at it. I've watched, and I'm telling you what I saw.
dialogue.conversations.standing.resume/2: The half that wasn't sure is smaller than it was. I count these things, apparently.
dialogue.conversations.standing.resume/3: Nothing's moved. I said years and I meant years, and you're a season in.
